Higher interest rates tend to make a currency more attractive to investors seeking better returns, thus boosting its value. Meanwhile, the Japanese yen, often considered a safe-haven asset, experienced a decline after a period of significant appreciation.

card.plain_headline: Canadian Dollar Drops on Weak Jobs Report
card.what_happened: The Canadian dollar weakened significantly after a disappointing jobs report indicated a slowdown in the Canadian economy. This weakness was amplified by strong US jobs data, which boosted the US dollar.
card.what_happened_verbose: The Canadian dollar experienced a notable decline against the US dollar following the release of Canada's latest employment figures. The data showed a much weaker-than-expected job creation number, suggesting a potential economic slowdown in Canada. This negative economic signal for Canada contrasted sharply with the robust US jobs report released concurrently, which bolstered the US dollar. The combination of domestic weakness and external strength in the US dollar put significant downward pressure on the Canadian currency.

source_item.title: U.S. 10-year Treasury yield spikes following blockbuster NFP report

card.plain_headline: Treasury Yields Jump on Strong Jobs Data
card.what_happened: Yields on US 10-year Treasury bonds rose sharply following a stronger-than-expected US jobs report. This indicates that investors anticipate higher interest rates for a longer period.
card.what_happened_verbose: The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note surged following the release of a 'blockbuster' Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report, which showed significantly more jobs were added than anticipated. Bond yields move inversely to bond prices. When a bond market expects higher interest rates or increased inflation, investors demand a higher yield to compensate for the diminished purchasing power of future coupon payments and the opportunity cost of holding lower-yielding assets. The strong jobs data fuels expectations that the Federal Reserve will likely keep interest rates higher for longer to manage inflation, leading to a sell-off in existing bonds and a rise in their yields.

affected.reason: Long-duration Treasury bonds are highly sensitive to rising interest rates, leading to price declines and yield increases.
Intermediate-term Treasury yields are also expected to rise, causing bond prices to fall.
Short-term Treasury yields will likely increase, but are less sensitive to long-term rate expectations than longer-duration bonds.

Robust foreign exchange reserves provide a buffer against external economic shocks, support the stability of the Indian Rupee, and signal strong international investor confidence in India's economic prospects. This record level suggests a healthy balance of payments and a strong position for the country in managing its international financial obligations.
